import unittest
from typing import Type
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
from flask.json.tag import TaggedJSONSerializer, JSONTag

class TestTaggedJSONSerializerRegister(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        """Set up a fresh serializer instance before each test."""
        self.serializer = TaggedJSONSerializer()
        
    def create_mock_tag_class(self, key: str = "test_tag") -> Type[JSONTag]:
        """Helper to create a mock tag class with a given key."""
        mock_tag_class = Mock(spec=JSONTag)
        mock_tag_instance = Mock()
        mock_tag_instance.key = key
        mock_tag_class.return_value = mock_tag_instance
        return mock_tag_class
    
    def test_register_new_tag_without_index(self):
        """Test registering a new tag without specifying an index (append)."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag")
        
        # Ensure tag is not already registered
        self.assertNotIn("new_tag", self.serializer.tags)
        initial_order_length = len(self.serializer.order)
        
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class)
        
        # Check that tag is registered
        self.assertIn("new_tag", self.serializer.tags)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.serializer.order), initial_order_length + 1)
        
        # Check that tag is appended to the end
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[-1].key, "new_tag")
        
        # Verify tag class was instantiated with serializer
        mock_tag_class.assert_called_once_with(self.serializer)
    
    def test_register_new_tag_with_index(self):
        """Test registering a new tag at a specific index."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag")
        
        # Insert at beginning
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class, index=0)
        
        self.assertIn("new_tag", self.serializer.tags)
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[0].key, "new_tag")
        
        # Insert at middle
        mock_tag_class2 = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag2")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class2, index=1)
        
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[1].key, "new_tag2")
    
    def test_register_existing_tag_without_force_raises_keyerror(self):
        """Test that registering an existing tag without force raises KeyError."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("existing_tag")
        
        # First registration should succeed
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class)
        
        # Second registration should fail
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class, force=False)
    
    def test_register_existing_tag_with_force_overwrites(self):
        """Test that registering an existing tag with force=True overwrites it."""
        mock_tag_class1 = self.create_mock_tag_class("test_tag")
        mock_tag_class2 = self.create_mock_tag_class("test_tag")
        
        # First registration
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class1)
        first_instance = self.serializer.tags["test_tag"]
        
        # Second registration with force
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class2, force=True)
        second_instance = self.serializer.tags["test_tag"]
        
        # Verify the tag was replaced
        self.assertNotEqual(first_instance, second_instance)
        
        # Verify order still contains only one instance of this tag
        tag_instances = [tag for tag in self.serializer.order if tag.key == "test_tag"]
        self.assertEqual(len(tag_instances), 1)
        self.assertEqual(tag_instances[0], second_instance)
    
    def test_register_preserves_order_when_force_replacing(self):
        """Test that order is preserved when replacing a tag with force=True."""
        # Create and register three tags
        tag_classes = []
        for i in range(3):
            tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class(f"tag{i}")
            tag_classes.append(tag_class)
            self.serializer.register(tag_class)
        
        # Replace middle tag with force
        replacement_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("tag1")
        self.serializer.register(replacement_tag_class, force=True)
        
        # Verify order is preserved: tag0, tag1, tag2
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[0].key, "tag0")
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[1].key, "tag1")
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[2].key, "tag2")
        
        # Verify the tag1 instance was replaced
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.tags["tag1"], replacement_tag_class.return_value)
    
    def test_register_with_negative_index(self):
        """Test registering with negative index (should work like list insert)."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag")
        
        # Register a tag at negative index (should insert before last element)
        # First add two default tags to have something to test against
        mock_tag_class1 = self.create_mock_tag_class("tag1")
        mock_tag_class2 = self.create_mock_tag_class("tag2")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class1)
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class2)
        
        # Insert at -1 (before last element)
        mock_tag_class3 = self.create_mock_tag_class("tag3")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class3, index=-1)
        
        # tag3 should be at position 1 (before tag2 at position 2)
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[1].key, "tag3")
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[2].key, "tag2")
    
    def test_register_with_index_out_of_bounds(self):
        """Test registering with index beyond list length (should append)."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag")
        
        # Register with index much larger than current length
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class, index=100)
        
        # Should be appended
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[-1].key, "new_tag")
        
        # Test with negative index beyond beginning
        mock_tag_class2 = self.create_mock_tag_class("new_tag2")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class2, index=-100)
        
        # Should be inserted at beginning
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[0].key, "new_tag2")
    
    def test_register_ensures_unique_keys_in_tags_dict(self):
        """Test that tags dict maintains unique keys."""
        # Register multiple tags
        for i in range(5):
            tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class(f"unique_tag{i}")
            self.serializer.register(tag_class)
        
        # Check all keys are unique in tags dict
        self.assertEqual(len(self.serializer.tags), 5)
        self.assertEqual(len(set(self.serializer.tags.keys())), 5)
    
    def test_register_maintains_order_invariants(self):
        """Test that order invariants are maintained after multiple registrations."""
        expected_order = []
        
        # Register 5 tags
        for i in range(5):
            tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class(f"tag{i}")
            self.serializer.register(tag_class)
            expected_order.append(f"tag{i}")
        
        # Verify order matches registration order
        actual_order = [tag.key for tag in self.serializer.order]
        self.assertEqual(actual_order, expected_order)
        
        # Insert a tag at position 2
        insert_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("inserted_tag")
        self.serializer.register(insert_tag_class, index=2)
        
        # Verify insertion worked
        actual_order = [tag.key for tag in self.serializer.order]
        expected_order.insert(2, "inserted_tag")
        self.assertEqual(actual_order, expected_order)
    
    def test_register_with_none_index_appends(self):
        """Test that index=None results in appending."""
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("appended_tag")
        
        # First add some tags
        for i in range(3):
            tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class(f"base_tag{i}")
            self.serializer.register(tag_class)
        
        initial_length = len(self.serializer.order)
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class, index=None)
        
        # Should be appended
        self.assertEqual(len(self.serializer.order), initial_length + 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.serializer.order[-1].key, "appended_tag")
    
    def test_register_invalid_tag_class_type(self):
        """Test that non-JSONTag classes raise appropriate errors."""
        class InvalidTagClass:
            pass
        
        with self.assertRaises((TypeError, AttributeError)):
            # Depending on implementation, this may raise TypeError or AttributeError
            self.serializer.register(InvalidTagClass)
    
    def test_register_with_existing_default_tags(self):
        """Test interaction with default tags that are registered in __init__."""
        # Count default tags
        default_tag_count = len(self.serializer.order)
        
        # Register a new tag
        mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class("custom_tag")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class)
        
        # Should have default_tags + 1
        self.assertEqual(len(self.serializer.order), default_tag_count + 1)
        
        # Try to force register a tag with same key as a default tag
        for default_tag in self.serializer.order[:-1]:  # Exclude our custom tag
            mock_tag_class = self.create_mock_tag_class(default_tag.key)
            self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class, force=True)
            
            # Should have replaced the default tag
            self.assertEqual(self.serializer.tags[default_tag.key], mock_tag_class.return_value)
    
    def test_register_clears_previous_order_entry_when_forced(self):
        """Test that when forcing replacement, the old instance is removed from order."""
        # Register initial tag
        mock_tag_class1 = self.create_mock_tag_class("test_tag")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class1)
        old_instance = self.serializer.tags["test_tag"]
        
        # Count occurrences in order
        old_count = sum(1 for tag in self.serializer.order if tag is old_instance)
        self.assertEqual(old_count, 1)
        
        # Force register new tag
        mock_tag_class2 = self.create_mock_tag_class("test_tag")
        self.serializer.register(mock_tag_class2, force=True)
        new_instance = self.serializer.tags["test_tag"]
        
        # Verify old instance is no longer in order
        new_count = sum(1 for tag in self.serializer.order if tag is old_instance)
        self.assertEqual(new_count, 0)
        
        # Verify new instance is in order exactly once
        new_count = sum(1 for tag in self.serializer.order if tag is new_instance)
        self.assertEqual(new_count, 1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

            # Call the original function

        return wrapper  # type: ignore

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures before each test method."""

        def original_func(scaffold_obj, *args, **kwargs):
            """Original function for testing."""
            return scaffold_obj, args, kwargs
        
        self.original_func = original_func
        
        # Create another test function with a specific return value
        def func_with_return(scaffold_obj, value):
            return value * 2
        
        self.func_with_return = func_with_return
        
        # Create a test function that raises an exception
        def func_that_raises(scaffold_obj, exc_type):
            raise exc_type("Test exception")
        
        self.func_that_raises = func_that_raises

        """Test that setupmethod returns a wrapped function."""
        decorated_func = setupmethod(self.original_func)

        # Verify it's not the original function
        self.assertIsNot(decorated_func, self.original_func)

        """Test that the wrapper preserves the original function's metadata."""
        decorated_func = setupmethod(self.original_func)

            self.original_func.__name__
        )

        expected_args = (1, 2)
        expected_kwargs = {'key': 'value'}

T_template_filter = TypeVar('T_template_filter', bound=Callable)

class TestAppDecorator(unittest.TestCase):
    
    def setUp(self):
        """Set up a fresh App instance for each test"""
        self.app = App(__name__)
    
    def test_decorator_registers_filter_with_explicit_name(self):
        """Test that decorator registers filter with explicit name parameter"""
        # Create a mock filter function
        def sample_filter(value):
            return value.upper()
        
        # Test with explicit name parameter
        with patch.object(self.app, 'add_template_filter') as mock_add:
            result = self.app.decorator(sample_filter)
            
            # Verify the filter was registered
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(sample_filter, None)
            
            # Verify the original function is returned
            self.assertEqual(result, sample_filter)
            
            # Verify function still works
            self.assertEqual(result('test'), 'TEST')
    
    def test_decorator_registers_filter_without_name(self):
        """Test that decorator registers filter without explicit name (uses function name)"""
        # Create a mock filter function
        def sample_filter(value):
            return value.lower()
        
        # Test without explicit name - decorator should use function name
        with patch.object(self.app, 'add_template_filter') as mock_add:
            result = self.app.decorator(sample_filter)
            
            # Verify the filter was registered
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(sample_filter, None)
            
            # Verify the original function is returned
            self.assertEqual(result, sample_filter)
    
    def test_decorator_returns_same_function_instance(self):
        """Test that decorator returns the exact same function instance"""
        # Create a filter function with specific identity
        def my_filter(x):
            return x * 2
        
        # Apply decorator
        result = self.app.decorator(my_filter)
        
        # Verify it's the same function object
        self.assertIs(result, my_filter)
    
    def test_decorator_preserves_function_behavior(self):
        """Test that the decorated function retains its original behavior"""
        # Create a complex filter function
        def complex_filter(data):
            if isinstance(data, list):
                return sum(data)
            elif isinstance(data, dict):
                return len(data)
            return str(data)
        
        # Apply decorator
        decorated = self.app.decorator(complex_filter)
        
        # Test various inputs to ensure behavior is preserved
        self.assertEqual(decorated([1, 2, 3]), 6)
        self.assertEqual(decorated({'a': 1, 'b': 2}), 2)
        self.assertEqual(decorated("test"), "test")
    
    def test_decorator_with_lambda_function(self):
        """Test that decorator works with lambda functions"""
        # Create a lambda filter
        lambda_filter = lambda x: x[::-1]  # reverse string
        
        # Apply decorator
        with patch.object(self.app, 'add_template_filter') as mock_add:
            result = self.app.decorator(lambda_filter)
            
            # Verify registration
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(lambda_filter, None)
            
            # Verify function behavior
            self.assertEqual(result('hello'), 'olleh')
    
    def test_decorator_with_class_method(self):
        """Test that decorator works with class methods"""
        # Create a class with a filter method
        class FilterClass:
            def filter_method(self, value):
                return value.title()
        
        instance = FilterClass()
        
        # Apply decorator to bound method
        with patch.object(self.app, 'add_template_filter') as mock_add:
            result = self.app.decorator(instance.filter_method)
            
            # Verify registration
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(instance.filter_method, None)
            
            # Verify function behavior
            self.assertEqual(result('hello world'), 'Hello World')

            return str(value)
        
        # Create a wrapper that adds functionality

            def inner(value):
                return f"PREFIX_{func(value)}_SUFFIX"
            return inner
        
        # Apply wrapper then decorator

            # Chain: wrapper then app.decorator

            # Verify registration
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(wrapped, None)
            
            # Verify chained behavior
            self.assertEqual(result(123), 'PREFIX_123_SUFFIX')

            # First registration

            # Verify both registrations occurred
            self.assertEqual(mock_add.call_count, 1)
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(shared_filter, None)
            
            # Both should return the same function
            self.assertIs(result1, shared_filter)
            self.assertIs(result2, shared_filter)

        # Verify function is returned

    def test_decorator_with_default_parameters(self):
        """Test that decorator works with functions having default parameters"""

        # Apply decorator
        with patch.object(self.app, 'add_template_filter') as mock_add:

            self.assertEqual(result(2, prefix='RESULT:'), 'RESULT:4')

import unittest
import tempfile
import os
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import importlib.util

# Import the App class from the correct module
from flask import Flask


class TestAppName(unittest.TestCase):
    """Test cases for the App.name property."""
    
    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        self.test_import_name = "test_app"
        self.app = Flask(self.test_import_name)
    
    def test_name_with_regular_import_name(self):
        """Test name property returns the import name when not '__main__'."""
        # Arrange
        expected_name = self.test_import_name
        
        # Act
        result = self.app.name
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(result, expected_name)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.name, self.app.import_name)
    
    def test_name_with_main_as_import_name(self):
        """Test name property returns derived name when import_name is '__main__'."""
        # Arrange
        # Create a temporary test file to simulate main module
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.py', delete=False) as tmp:
            temp_file = tmp.name
        
        try:
            # Mock the __main__ module
            with patch.object(self.app, 'import_name', '__main__'):
                # Mock sys.modules['__main__'] to have a __file__ attribute
                with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'__main__': MagicMock(__file__=temp_file)}):
                    # Act
                    result = self.app.name
                    
                    # Assert - should derive name from file path
                    expected_name = Path(temp_file).stem
                    self.assertEqual(result, expected_name)
        finally:
            # Cleanup
            if os.path.exists(temp_file):
                os.unlink(temp_file)
    
    def test_name_with_main_and_no_file_attribute(self):
        """Test name property returns '__main__' when main module has no __file__."""
        # Arrange
        with patch.object(self.app, 'import_name', '__main__'):
            # Mock sys.modules['__main__'] without __file__ attribute
            mock_main = MagicMock()
            del mock_main.__file__
            with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'__main__': mock_main}):
                # Act
                result = self.app.name
                
                # Assert - should fall back to '__main__'
                self.assertEqual(result, '__main__')
    
    def test_name_caching_behavior(self):
        """Test that name property returns consistent value (potentially cached)."""
        # Arrange
        expected_name = self.test_import_name
        
        # Act - call multiple times
        result1 = self.app.name
        result2 = self.app.name
        result3 = self.app.name
        
        # Assert - all calls should return the same value
        self.assertEqual(result1, expected_name)
        self.assertEqual(result2, expected_name)
        self.assertEqual(result3, expected_name)
        self.assertEqual(result1, result2)
        self.assertEqual(result2, result3)
    
    def test_name_with_different_import_names(self):
        """Test name property with various import name patterns."""
        test_cases = [
            ("myapp", "myapp"),
            ("my_app", "my_app"),
            ("my-app", "my-app"),
            ("my.app", "my.app"),
            ("123app", "123app"),
            ("app_123", "app_123"),
        ]
        
        for import_name, expected_name in test_cases:
            with self.subTest(import_name=import_name):
                # Arrange
                app = Flask(import_name)
                
                # Act
                result = app.name
                
                # Assert
                self.assertEqual(result, expected_name)
    
    def test_name_does_not_modify_app_state(self):
        """Test that accessing name property doesn't modify app instance state."""
        # Arrange
        initial_state = {
            'import_name': self.app.import_name,
            'config': dict(self.app.config),
            'blueprints': dict(self.app.blueprints),
            'extensions': dict(self.app.extensions),
        }
        
        # Act
        name_result = self.app.name
        name_result2 = self.app.name  # Call twice to check for side effects
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(self.app.import_name, initial_state['import_name'])
        self.assertDictEqual(dict(self.app.config), initial_state['config'])
        self.assertDictEqual(self.app.blueprints, initial_state['blueprints'])
        self.assertDictEqual(self.app.extensions, initial_state['extensions'])
        self.assertEqual(name_result, name_result2)
    
    def test_name_when_main_module_is_package(self):
        """Test name derivation when __main__ is a package __init__.py file."""
        # Arrange
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            package_dir = os.path.join(temp_dir, "mypackage")
            init_file = os.path.join(package_dir, "__init__.py")
            
            # Create package structure
            os.makedirs(package_dir)
            with open(init_file, 'w') as f:
                f.write("# Package init")
            
            with patch.object(self.app, 'import_name', '__main__'):
                # Mock __main__ with __init__.py file
                with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'__main__': MagicMock(__file__=init_file)}):
                    # Act
                    result = self.app.name
                    
                    # Assert - should use directory name, not "__init__"
                    expected_name = "mypackage"
                    self.assertEqual(result, expected_name)
    
    def test_name_with_unicode_import_name(self):
        """Test name property handles unicode characters in import name."""
        # Arrange
        unicode_import_name = "my_app_测试"
        app = Flask(unicode_import_name)
        
        # Act
        result = app.name
        
        # Assert
        self.assertEqual(result, unicode_import_name)
    
    def test_name_property_is_string(self):
        """Test that name property always returns a string."""
        # Arrange & Act
        result = self.app.name
        
        # Assert
        self.assertIsInstance(result, str)
        self.assertGreater(len(result), 0)

import unittest
import sys
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
from flask import Flask
from flask.cli import locate_app, NoAppException

class TestLocateApp(unittest.TestCase):
    
    def setUp(self):
        # Clear any test modules that might have been added
        self.modules_to_clean = []
        
    def tearDown(self):
        # Remove test modules from sys.modules
        for module_name in self.modules_to_clean:
            if module_name in sys.modules:
                del sys.modules[module_name]
    
    def create_test_module(self, module_name, app_name=None, app_instance=None, multiple_apps=None):
        """Helper to create a test module in sys.modules"""
        module = MagicMock()
        
        if multiple_apps:
            for app_key, app_obj in multiple_apps.items():
                setattr(module, app_key, app_obj)
        elif app_name and app_instance:
            setattr(module, app_name, app_instance)
        elif app_instance:
            # Single app without specific name
            setattr(module, 'app', app_instance)
            setattr(module, 'application', app_instance)
            setattr(module, 'create_app', MagicMock(return_value=app_instance))
        
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)
        return module
    
    def test_locate_app_with_explicit_app_name(self):
        """Test locating app with specific app name"""
        module_name = 'test_module_explicit'
        app_name = 'my_app'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        self.create_test_module(module_name, app_name=app_name, app_instance=test_app)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, app_name)
        self.assertIs(result, test_app)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_none_app_name_finds_best_app(self):
        """Test locating app with None app name finds best candidate"""
        module_name = 'test_module_best'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        module = self.create_test_module(module_name, app_instance=test_app)
        # Add multiple app-like attributes
        setattr(module, 'app', test_app)
        setattr(module, 'application', test_app)
        setattr(module, 'create_app', MagicMock(return_value=test_app))
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, None)
        self.assertIs(result, test_app)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_none_app_name_no_app_found(self):
        """Test locating app with None app name when no app found returns None"""
        module_name = 'test_module_no_app'
        
        # Create module without Flask app
        module = MagicMock()
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, None, raise_if_not_found=False)
        self.assertIsNone(result)
    
    def test_locate_app_raises_no_app_exception_when_module_not_found(self):
        """Test that NoAppException is raised when module cannot be imported"""
        module_name = 'non_existent_module'
        
        with self.assertRaises(NoAppException):
            locate_app(module_name, 'some_app')
    
    def test_locate_app_returns_none_when_module_not_found_and_raise_false(self):
        """Test returns None when module not found and raise_if_not_found=False"""
        module_name = 'another_non_existent_module'
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, 'some_app', raise_if_not_found=False)
        self.assertIsNone(result)
    
    def test_locate_app_raises_no_app_exception_when_specific_app_not_found(self):
        """Test NoAppException when specific app name not found in module"""
        module_name = 'test_module_no_specific_app'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        self.create_test_module(module_name, app_instance=test_app)
        
        with self.assertRaises(NoAppException):
            locate_app(module_name, 'non_existent_app')
    
    def test_locate_app_returns_none_when_specific_app_not_found_and_raise_false(self):
        """Test returns None when specific app not found and raise_if_not_found=False"""
        module_name = 'test_module_no_specific_app2'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        self.create_test_module(module_name, app_instance=test_app)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, 'non_existent_app', raise_if_not_found=False)
        self.assertIsNone(result)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_create_app_function(self):
        """Test locating app when module has create_app function"""
        module_name = 'test_module_create_app'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        module = MagicMock()
        module.create_app = MagicMock(return_value=test_app)
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, None)
        self.assertIs(result, test_app)
        module.create_app.assert_called_once()
    
    def test_locate_app_prefers_app_over_application(self):
        """Test that 'app' is preferred over 'application' when both exist"""
        module_name = 'test_module_preference'
        test_app1 = Flask('test_app1')
        test_app2 = Flask('test_app2')
        
        module = MagicMock()
        module.app = test_app1
        module.application = test_app2
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, None)
        self.assertIs(result, test_app1)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_multiple_apps_and_specific_name(self):
        """Test locating specific app when multiple apps exist in module"""
        module_name = 'test_module_multiple'
        test_app1 = Flask('test_app1')
        test_app2 = Flask('test_app2')
        test_app3 = Flask('test_app3')
        
        self.create_test_module(
            module_name,
            multiple_apps={
                'app1': test_app1,
                'app2': test_app2,
                'app3': test_app3
            }
        )
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, 'app2')
        self.assertIs(result, test_app2)

            with self.assertRaises(NoAppException):
                locate_app(module_name, 'some_app', raise_if_not_found=True)

            result = locate_app(module_name, 'some_app', raise_if_not_found=False)
            self.assertIsNone(result)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_empty_module(self):
        """Test locating app from completely empty module"""

        module = MagicMock()
        # Module has no attributes at all
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)

        self.assertIsNone(result)
        
        with self.assertRaises(NoAppException):
            locate_app(module_name, None, raise_if_not_found=True)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_app_as_attribute_not_callable(self):
        """Test when app attribute exists but is not a Flask instance"""
        module_name = 'non_flask_module'
        
        module = MagicMock()
        module.app = "not a flask app"
        sys.modules[module_name] = module
        self.modules_to_clean.append(module_name)
        
        result = locate_app(module_name, None, raise_if_not_found=False)
        self.assertIsNone(result)
    
    def test_locate_app_module_already_imported(self):
        """Test locating app from already imported module"""
        module_name = 'pre_imported_module'
        test_app = Flask('test_app')
        
        # Import the module first
        self.create_test_module(module_name, app_instance=test_app)
        
        # Now locate app - should work without re-importing
        result = locate_app(module_name, None)
        self.assertIs(result, test_app)
    
    def test_locate_app_with_app_name_none_and_module_has_no_flask_apps(self):
        """Test when app_name is None but module has objects that are not Flask apps"""

                # Verify FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI was set

class TestBlueprintDecorator(unittest.TestCase):

        from flask.sansio.blueprints import Blueprint

        bp = Blueprint(name="bp", import_name=__name__)
        calls = {}

        def fake_add_app_template_global(self_ref, f, name=None):
            calls['f'] = f
            calls['name'] = name

        bp.add_app_template_global = fake_add_app_template_global.__get__(bp, Blueprint)

        @bp.decorator
        def some_function():
            return "hello"

        self.assertIs(calls.get('f'), some_function)
        self.assertIn('name', calls)
        self.assertIsInstance(calls['name'], str)

    def test_decorator_returns_same_function(self):
        from flask.sansio.blueprints import Blueprint

        bp = Blueprint(name="bp_return", import_name=__name__)
        def f_to_decorate():
            pass

        result = bp.decorator(f_to_decorate)
        self.assertIs(result, f_to_decorate)

    def test_init_raises_on_empty_name(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as cm:
            Blueprint(name="", import_name=__name__)
        self.assertIn("'name' may not be empty.", str(cm.exception))

    def test_init_raises_on_dot_in_name(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as cm:
            Blueprint(name="invalid.name", import_name=__name__)
        self.assertIn("'name' may not contain a dot '.' character.", str(cm.exception))

        bp = Blueprint(name="valid", import_name=__name__)
        self.assertEqual(bp.name, "valid")
        self.assertIsNone(bp.url_prefix)
        self.assertIsNone(bp.subdomain)
        self.assertIsNone(bp.root_path)

from werkzeug.test import EnvironBuilder


class TestOpen(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.app = Flask(__name__)

        @self.app.route("/")
        def index():
            return jsonify({"ok": True})

        self.client = self.app.test_client()

    def test_open_with_environ_builder(self):
        builder = EnvironBuilder(path="/", method="GET")
        resp = self.client.open(builder, buffered=True)
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.get_json(), {"ok": True})

    def test_open_with_environ_dict(self):
        environ = {
            "PATH_INFO": "/",
            "REQUEST_METHOD": "GET",
            "wsgi.url_scheme": "http",
            "SERVER_NAME": "localhost",
            "SERVER_PORT": "80",
            "SCRIPT_NAME": "",
            "QUERY_STRING": "",
            "wsgi.input": io.BytesIO(b""),
            "wsgi.errors": io.StringIO(),
            "SERVER_PROTOCOL": "HTTP/1.1",
            "REMOTE_ADDR": "127.0.0.1",
            "CONTENT_LENGTH": "0",
            "CONTENT_TYPE": "",
            "wsgi.version": (1, 0),
            "wsgi.multithread": True,
            "wsgi.multiprocess": False,
        }
        resp = self.client.open(environ)
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.get_json(), {"ok": True})

    def test_open_with_base_request(self):
        builder = EnvironBuilder(path="/", method="GET")
        req = builder.get_request()
        resp = self.client.open(req)
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.get_json(), {"ok": True})

    def test_open_with_path_argument(self):
        resp = self.client.open("/")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.get_json(), {"ok": True})

    def test_new_contexts_reentered(self):
        app = Flask(__name__)

        @app.route("/")
        def index():
            return jsonify({"ok": True})

        client = app.test_client()

        log = []

        class DummyCtx:
            def __enter__(self):
                log.append(("enter", "ctx"))
                return self

            def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
                log.append(("exit", "ctx"))
                return False

        dummy = DummyCtx()
        client._new_contexts.append(dummy)

        resp = client.open("/")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(log, [("enter", "ctx")])

def dummy_url_defaults(endpoint, values):

        assert self.scaffold.url_default_functions[None] == []

        values = {}
        for func in self.scaffold.url_default_functions[None]:
            func(endpoint, values)

        # Check if the values were modified
        assert values['lang'] == 'en'

import pytest
from flask.sansio.blueprints import Blueprint

class TestBlueprintAppTemplateGlobal:
    
    def setup_method(self):
        self.blueprint = Blueprint(name="test_blueprint", import_name=__name__)

    def test_app_template_global_with_function(self):
        def sample_function():
            return "Hello, World!"

        decorator = self.blueprint.app_template_global()
        result = decorator(sample_function)
        assert result is sample_function
        assert "sample_function" in self.blueprint.deferred_functions
        self.blueprint.deferred_functions[0](self.blueprint)
        assert "sample_function" in self.blueprint.jinja_globals
        assert self.blueprint.jinja_globals["sample_function"]() == "Hello, World!"

    def test_app_template_global_with_name(self):
        def sample_function():
            return "Hello, World!"

        decorator = self.blueprint.app_template_global("custom_name")
        result = decorator(sample_function)
        assert result is sample_function
        assert "custom_name" not in self.blueprint.jinja_globals
        self.blueprint.deferred_functions[0](self.blueprint)
        assert "custom_name" in self.blueprint.jinja_globals
        assert self.blueprint.jinja_globals["custom_name"]() == "Hello, World!"

    def test_app_template_global_with_invalid_name(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="may not contain a dot"):
            self.blueprint.app_template_global("invalid.name")

    def test_app_template_global_direct_call(self):
        def sample_function():
            return "Hello, World!"

        result = self.blueprint.app_template_global(sample_function)
        assert result is sample_function
        assert "sample_function" not in self.blueprint.jinja_globals
        self.blueprint.deferred_functions[0](self.blueprint)
        assert "sample_function" in self.blueprint.jinja_globals
        assert self.blueprint.jinja_globals["sample_function"]() == "Hello, World!"

    with app.app_context():

            mock_init.assert_called_once()

    with app.app_context():

from flask import Flask, request
from flask.views import MethodView
from werkzeug.exceptions import MethodNotAllowed

class MockMethodView(MethodView):
    def get(self, **kwargs):
        return "GET response", 200

    def post(self, **kwargs):
        return "POST response", 201

    def head(self, **kwargs):
        return "HEAD response", 200

class TestDispatchRequest:

    def app(self):
        app = Flask(__name__)
        app.add_url_rule('/mock', view_func=MockMethodView.as_view('mock'))

    def test_dispatch_request_get(self, app):
        with app.test_request_context('/mock', method='GET'):
            view = MockMethodView()
            response = view.dispatch_request()
            assert response == "GET response"

        with app.test_request_context('/mock', method='POST'):
            view = MockMethodView()
            response = view.dispatch_request()
            assert response == "POST response"

    def test_dispatch_request_head(self, app):
        with app.test_request_context('/mock', method='HEAD'):
            view = MockMethodView()
            response = view.dispatch_request()
            assert response == "HEAD response"

from flask.sansio.scaffold import Scaffold


def test_decorator_registers_rule_with_endpoint_and_options():
    s = Scaffold(import_name=__name__, root_path=".")
    captured = {}

    def fake_add_url_rule(self, rule, endpoint=None, view_func=None, **options):
        captured['rule'] = rule
        captured['endpoint'] = endpoint
        captured['view_func'] = view_func
        captured['options'] = options

    s.add_url_rule = types.MethodType(fake_add_url_rule, s)

    def view():
        return "ok"

    decorator = s.route('/test', endpoint='test', methods=['GET'])
    ret = decorator(view)

    assert ret is view
    assert captured['rule'] == '/test'
    assert captured['endpoint'] == 'test'
    assert captured['view_func'] is view
    assert captured['options'] == {'methods': ['GET']}


def test_decorator_raises_keyerror_when_endpoint_missing():
    s = Scaffold(import_name=__name__, root_path=".")

    def fake_add_url_rule(self, rule, endpoint=None, view_func=None, **options):
        pass

    s.add_url_rule = types.MethodType(fake_add_url_rule, s)

    def view():
        pass

    decorator = s.route('/missing')  # no endpoint provided

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        decorator(view)

    sc.url_defaults(f)

    last = sc.url_default_functions[None][-1]
    endpoint = "view_endpoint"

    assert values["added"] == 123

import io

from flask.json import load

class FakeProvider:
    def __init__(self):
        self.last_fp = None
        self.last_kwargs = None

    def load(self, fp, **kwargs):
        self.last_fp = fp
        self.last_kwargs = kwargs
        content = fp.read()
        try:
            fp.seek(0)
        except Exception:
            pass
        return json.loads(content, **kwargs)

class Test__init__:

    def test_load_without_app_context_preserves_fp_and_parses_json(self):

        assert fp.tell() == initial_pos

    def test_load_with_app_context_uses_provider_and_preserves_fp_position(self):
        app = Flask(__name__)
        app.json = FakeProvider()
        with app.app_context():
            fp = io.StringIO('{"b": 2}')
            initial_pos = fp.tell()

import pytest
from unittest.mock import Mock
from flask.json.tag import TagDict

class TestToJSON:
    def test_to_json_with_valid_dict(self):
        # Arrange
        serializer_mock = Mock()
        serializer_mock.tag.return_value = "serialized_value"
        
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = serializer_mock
        
        input_value = {"key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"}
        
        # Act
        result = tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
        
        # Assert
        assert result == {"key1__": "serialized_value"}
        serializer_mock.tag.assert_called_once_with("value1")
    
    def test_to_json_with_empty_dict_raises_stop_iteration(self):
        # Arrange
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = Mock()
        input_value = {}
        
        # Act & Assert
        with pytest.raises(StopIteration):
            tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
    
    def test_to_json_with_serializer_missing_tag_method_raises_attribute_error(self):
        # Arrange
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = Mock(spec=[])  # No tag method
        input_value = {"key1": "value1"}
        
        # Act & Assert
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
    
    def test_to_json_with_none_value(self):
        # Arrange
        serializer_mock = Mock()
        serializer_mock.tag.return_value = None
        
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = serializer_mock
        
        input_value = {"key1": None}
        
        # Act
        result = tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
        
        # Assert
        assert result == {"key1__": None}
        serializer_mock.tag.assert_called_once_with(None)
    
    def test_to_json_with_nested_dict_value(self):
        # Arrange
        serializer_mock = Mock()
        serialized_result = {"nested": "dict"}
        serializer_mock.tag.return_value = serialized_result
        
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = serializer_mock
        
        input_value = {"key1": {"inner_key": "inner_value"}}
        
        # Act
        result = tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
        
        # Assert
        assert result == {"key1__": serialized_result}
        serializer_mock.tag.assert_called_once_with({"inner_key": "inner_value"})
    
    def test_to_json_calls_serializer_tag_with_first_value_only(self):
        # Arrange
        serializer_mock = Mock()
        serializer_mock.tag.return_value = "serialized"
        
        tag_dict = TagDict()
        tag_dict.serializer = serializer_mock

        # Act
        result = tag_dict.to_json(input_value)
        
        # Assert
        assert result == {"key1__": "serialized"}
        serializer_mock.tag.assert_called_once_with("value1")

import pytest
from unittest.mock import Mock
from flask.sansio.scaffold import Scaffold
import os

class TestScaffoldUrlDefaults:

    def test_url_defaults_registration(self):
        """Test that url_defaults properly registers a function"""
        scaffold = Scaffold(import_name="test_app")
        mock_func = Mock()
        
        # Register the function
        result = scaffold.url_defaults(mock_func)
        
        # Verify the function is returned (for chaining)
        assert result is mock_func
        
        # Verify the function is added to url_default_functions
        assert mock_func in scaffold.url_default_functions[None]

    def test_url_defaults_multiple_registrations(self):
        """Test that multiple functions can be registered"""
        scaffold = Scaffold(import_name="test_app")
        func1 = Mock()
        func2 = Mock()
        func3 = Mock()
        
        scaffold.url_defaults(func1)
        scaffold.url_defaults(func2)
        scaffold.url_defaults(func3)
        
        # All functions should be in the list
        assert func1 in scaffold.url_default_functions[None]
        assert func2 in scaffold.url_default_functions[None]
        assert func3 in scaffold.url_default_functions[None]
        
        # Verify order is maintained
        funcs = scaffold.url_default_functions[None]
        assert funcs.index(func1) < funcs.index(func2)
        assert funcs.index(func2) < funcs.index(func3)

    def test_url_defaults_with_different_import_names(self):
        """Test url_defaults works with different import names"""
        scaffold1 = Scaffold(import_name="app1")
        scaffold2 = Scaffold(import_name="app2")
        func1 = Mock()
        func2 = Mock()
        
        scaffold1.url_defaults(func1)
        scaffold2.url_defaults(func2)
        
        assert func1 in scaffold1.url_default_functions[None]
        assert func2 in scaffold2.url_default_functions[None]
        
        # Functions should not be shared between instances
        assert func2 not in scaffold1.url_default_functions[None]
        assert func1 not in scaffold2.url_default_functions[None]

    def test_url_defaults_function_signature_compatibility(self):
        """Test that the registered function maintains its signature characteristics"""
        scaffold = Scaffold(import_name="test_app")
        
        def sample_url_default(endpoint, values):
            values['test'] = 'value'
            return values
            
        # Register the function
        result = scaffold.url_defaults(sample_url_default)
        
        # Should return the same function
        assert result is sample_url_default
        
        # Should be callable with expected parameters
        test_values = {}
        result('test_endpoint', test_values)
        assert test_values == {'test': 'value'}

    def test_url_defaults_initialization_state(self):
        """Test that url_default_functions is properly initialized"""
        scaffold = Scaffold(import_name="test_app")
        
        # url_default_functions should be initialized as a defaultdict
        assert hasattr(scaffold.url_default_functions, '__getitem__')
        
        # None key should exist and be a list
        assert isinstance(scaffold.url_default_functions[None], list)
        
        # Initially empty
        assert len(scaffold.url_default_functions[None]) == 0

    def test_url_defaults_preserves_existing_functions(self):
        """Test that registering new functions doesn't remove existing ones"""
        scaffold = Scaffold(import_name="test_app")
        existing_func = Mock()
        
        # Manually add a function

from flask.views import View
from flask import Flask, current_app
from flask.typing import ResponseReturnValue

class TestView(View):
    def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs) -> ResponseReturnValue:
        return f"Test response with {kwargs}"


class TestViewMethod:
    
    @pytest.fixture
    def app(self):
        app = Flask(__name__)
        app.config['TESTING'] = True
        return app

    def test_view_success(self, app):
        with app.app_context():
            # Arrange
            kwargs = {'param1': 'value1', 'param2': 'value2'}
            
            # Act
            result = TestView.as_view('test_view', **kwargs)()
            
            # Assert
            # Since as_view creates a function, we're testing that it executes without error
            assert callable(result) or isinstance(result, str)

    @patch('flask.views.current_app')
    def test_view_with_current_app_mock(self, mock_current_app):
        # Arrange
        mock_app = Mock()
        mock_current_app._get_current_object.return_value = mock_app
        mock_app.ensure_sync.return_value = lambda f: f
        
        view_instance = TestView()
        with patch.object(TestView, '__new__', return_value=view_instance):
            with patch.object(view_instance, 'dispatch_request', return_value="Mocked response") as mock_dispatch:
                
                # Act
                result = TestView.as_view('test_view')()
                
                # Assert
                mock_dispatch.assert_called_once()

    def test_view_incorrect_view_class(self):
        # Arrange
        class IncompleteView(View):
            pass  # No dispatch_request method
        
        # Act & Assert
        with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
            IncompleteView.as_view('incomplete_view')()

    def test_view_with_decorators(self, app):
        # Arrange
        def simple_decorator(f):
            def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                return f"Decorated: {f(*args, **kwargs)}"
            return wrapper
            
        class DecoratedView(View):
            decorators = [simple_decorator]
            
            def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs) -> ResponseReturnValue:
                return "Original response"
        
        with app.app_context():
            # Act
            view_func = DecoratedView.as_view('decorated_view')
            result = view_func()
            
            # Assert
            assert "Decorated:" in result
            assert "Original response" in result

    def test_view_init_every_request_true(self, app):
        with app.app_context():
            # Arrange
            init_count = 0
            
            class CounterView(View):
                def __init__(self):
                    super().__init__()
                    nonlocal init_count
                    init_count += 1
                    
                def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs) -> ResponseReturnValue:
                    return f"Init count: {init_count}"
            
            view_func = CounterView.as_view('counter_view')
            
            # Act
            result1 = view_func()
            result2 = view_func()
            
            # Assert
            assert init_count == 2  # Should be instantiated twice

    def test_view_init_every_request_false(self, app):
        with app.app_context():
            # Arrange
            init_count = 0
            
            class SingleInitView(View):
                init_every_request = False
                
                def __init__(self):
                    super().__init__()
                    nonlocal init_count
                    init_count += 1
                    
                def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs) -> ResponseReturnValue:
                    return f"Init count: {init_count}"
            
            view_func = SingleInitView.as_view('single_init_view')
            
            # Act
            result1 = view_func()
            result2 = view_func()
            
            # Assert
            assert init_count == 1  # Should be instantiated only once

class TestFlaskCliRunnerInvoke:

        assert result.exit_code == 0

        expected = '{\n  "key": "value"\n}'
        assert result == expected

        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.ensure_ascii = False
        result = provider.dumps({"key": "value 🚀"})
        assert result == '{"key": "value 🚀"}'

    def test_serialization_with_ensure_ascii_true(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.ensure_ascii = True
        result = provider.dumps({"key": "value 🚀"})
        # Should escape non-ASCII characters
        assert "\\ud83d\\ude80" in result

    def test_serialization_with_sort_keys_true(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.sort_keys = True
        result = provider.dumps({"b": 1, "a": 2})
        assert result == '{"a": 2, "b": 1}'

    def test_serialization_with_sort_keys_false(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.sort_keys = False
        result = provider.dumps({"b": 1, "a": 2})
        # Order may vary, but should contain both keys
        assert '"b": 1' in result
        assert '"a": 2' in result

        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        
        class CustomObject:
            def __str__(self):
                return "custom"
        
        # Override the default function
        def custom_default(obj):
            if isinstance(obj, CustomObject):
                return str(obj)
            raise TypeError(f"Object of type {type(obj)} is not JSON serializable")
        
        provider.default = custom_default
        obj = CustomObject()
        result = provider.dumps({"custom": obj})
        assert result == '{"custom": "custom"}'

    def test_serialization_compact_format(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.compact = True
        result = provider.dumps({"key": "value"})
        assert result == '{"key":"value"}'  # No extra spaces

    def test_serialization_non_compact_format(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.compact = False
        result = provider.dumps({"key": "value"})
        assert result == '{ "key": "value" }'  # With spaces

    def test_serialization_with_none_compact_uses_default_spacing(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        provider.compact = None
        result = provider.dumps({"key": "value"})
        # Should use default json.dumps spacing (single space after separators)
        assert result == '{"key": "value"}'

    def test_calls_internal_default_function(self, mock_default):

            pass
            
        obj = UnserializableObject()
        try:

        except:
            pass
            
        # Verify that _default was called with the object
        mock_default.assert_called()

    def test_serialization_of_various_types(self):
        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)

        assert parsed == test_obj

        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        original_obj = {"key": ["value1", "value2"]}

        provider.dumps(original_obj)
        assert original_obj == original_copy  # Original object unchanged

        provider = DefaultJSONProvider(None)
        # Even though sort_keys is True by default, kwargs should override
        result = provider.dumps({"b": 1, "a": 2}, sort_keys=False)
        # Order may vary, but should contain both keys
        assert '"b": 1' in result
        assert '"a": 2' in result

        assert result == '{"key": "🚀"}'

import os
import tempfile
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock
import pytest
from flask import Flask, Response
from flask.blueprints import Blueprint


class TestSendStaticFile:

    @pytest.fixture
    def temp_static_dir(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            yield temp_dir

    @pytest.fixture
    def blueprint_with_static(self, temp_static_dir):
        bp = Blueprint('test_bp', __name__, static_folder=temp_static_dir)
        return bp

    @pytest.fixture
    def app(self):
        return Flask(__name__)

    def test_send_static_file_success(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        # Create a test file
        test_file_path = os.path.join(temp_static_dir, 'test.txt')
        with open(test_file_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('Hello, World!')

        # Register blueprint to app to avoid context issues
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with app.test_request_context():
            response = blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('test.txt')
            
        assert isinstance(response, Response)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.get_data(as_text=True) == 'Hello, World!'

    def test_send_static_file_not_found(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with app.test_request_context():
            with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
                blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('nonexistent.txt')

    def test_send_static_file_no_static_folder(self):
        bp = Blueprint('test_bp', __name__)  # No static folder provided
        
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="No static folder for this blueprint"):
            bp.send_static_file('anyfile.txt')

    def test_send_static_file_with_caching_headers(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        # Create a test file
        test_file_path = os.path.join(temp_static_dir, 'cached.js')
        with open(test_file_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('console.log("test");')
            
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with patch.object(blueprint_with_static, 'get_send_file_max_age', return_value=3600):
            with app.test_request_context():
                response = blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('cached.js')
                
        assert 'Cache-Control' in response.headers
        assert 'max-age=3600' in response.headers['Cache-Control']

    def test_send_static_file_directory_traversal_prevention(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with app.test_request_context():
            with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
                # This should be blocked to prevent directory traversal
                blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('../etc/passwd')

    def test_send_static_file_empty_filename(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with app.test_request_context():
            with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
                blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('')

    def test_send_static_file_with_subdirectory(self, blueprint_with_static, temp_static_dir, app):
        # Create a subdirectory and file
        subdir = os.path.join(temp_static_dir, 'subdir')
        os.makedirs(subdir)
        test_file_path = os.path.join(subdir, 'nested.txt')
        with open(test_file_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write('Nested file content')
            
        app.register_blueprint(blueprint_with_static)
        
        with app.test_request_context():
            response = blueprint_with_static.send_static_file('subdir/nested.txt')
            
        assert isinstance(response, Response)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.get_data(as_text=True) == 'Nested file content'

from flask.blueprints import Blueprint


class TestOpenResource:
    @pytest.fixture
    def blueprint(self):

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
            bp = Blueprint("test_bp", __name__, root_path=temp_dir)
            yield bp

    @pytest.fixture
    def sample_file(self, blueprint):
        """Create a sample file in the blueprint's root path."""
        file_path = Path(blueprint.root_path) / "sample.txt"
        file_path.write_text("Hello, World!", encoding="utf-8")
        return "sample.txt"

    def test_open_resource_default_mode(self, blueprint, sample_file):
        """Test opening a resource with default binary mode."""
        with blueprint.open_resource(sample_file) as f:
            assert f.mode == "rb"
            content = f.read()
            assert isinstance(content, bytes)
            assert b"Hello, World!" in content

    def test_open_resource_text_mode(self, blueprint, sample_file):
        """Test opening a resource in text mode."""
        with blueprint.open_resource(sample_file, mode="r") as f:
            assert f.mode == "r"
            content = f.read()
            assert isinstance(content, str)
            assert "Hello, World!" in content

    def test_open_resource_text_mode_explicit_encoding(self, blueprint, sample_file):
        """Test opening a resource in text mode with explicit encoding."""
        with blueprint.open_resource(sample_file, mode="rt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            assert f.mode == "rt"
            content = f.read()
            assert isinstance(content, str)
            assert "Hello, World!" in content

    def test_open_resource_binary_mode_ignores_encoding(self, blueprint, sample_file):
        """Test that encoding is ignored in binary mode."""
        with blueprint.open_resource(sample_file, mode="rb", encoding="latin-1") as f:
            assert f.mode == "rb"
            content = f.read()
            assert isinstance(content, bytes)

    def test_open_resource_invalid_mode_raises_value_error(self, blueprint):
        """Test that invalid modes raise ValueError."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Invalid mode"):
            blueprint.open_resource("nonexistent.txt", mode="w")

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Invalid mode"):
            blueprint.open_resource("nonexistent.txt", mode="a")

        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Invalid mode"):
            blueprint.open_resource("nonexistent.txt", mode="wb")

    def test_open_resource_nonexistent_file_raises_file_not_found(self, blueprint):
        """Test that nonexistent files raise FileNotFoundError."""
        with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
            with blueprint.open_resource("nonexistent.txt") as f:
                pass

    def test_open_resource_with_subdirectory(self, blueprint):
        """Test opening a resource in a subdirectory."""

                self.serializer = serializer_instance

                return value

import unittest
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
from flask.sansio.blueprints import Blueprint

class TestBlueprintDecorator(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self.blueprint = Blueprint('test_bp', '__name__')

    def test_decorator_registers_function_as_template_global(self):
        mock_func = Mock(__name__='test_func')
        
        with patch.object(self.blueprint, 'add_app_template_global') as mock_add:
            decorated_func = self.blueprint.decorator(mock_func)
            
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(mock_func, name='test_func')
            self.assertEqual(decorated_func, mock_func)

    def test_decorator_preserves_function_attributes(self):
        def test_func():
            return "test"
        
        test_func.custom_attr = "custom_value"
        
        with patch.object(self.blueprint, 'add_app_template_global'):
            decorated_func = self.blueprint.decorator(test_func)
            
            self.assertEqual(decorated_func.custom_attr, "custom_value")
            self.assertEqual(decorated_func(), "test")

    def test_decorator_with_lambda_function(self):
        lambda_func = lambda x: x * 2
        
        with patch.object(self.blueprint, 'add_app_template_global') as mock_add:
            decorated_func = self.blueprint.decorator(lambda_func)
            
            mock_add.assert_called_once()
            self.assertEqual(decorated_func(5), 10)

    def test_decorator_with_function_without_name(self):
        mock_func = Mock()
        del mock_func.__name__
        
        with patch.object(self.blueprint, 'add_app_template_global') as mock_add:
            decorated_func = self.blueprint.decorator(mock_func)
            
            mock_add.assert_called_once_with(mock_func, name=None)
            self.assertEqual(decorated_func, mock_func)

    def test_decorator_returns_same_function_object(self):
        def original_func():
            pass
        
        original_id = id(original_func)
        
        with patch.object(self.blueprint, 'add_app_template_global'):
            decorated_func = self.blueprint.decorator(original_func)
            
            self.assertEqual(id(decorated_func), original_id)
            self.assertIs(decorated_func, original_func)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import os

class TestAppTemplateGlobal(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up a basic Blueprint instance for testing."""
        self.blueprint = Blueprint(
            name="test_blueprint",
            import_name=__name__,
            template_folder="templates"
        )

    def test_app_template_global_with_name_provided(self):
        """Test registering a template global with a specific name."""
        def test_func():
            return "global_value"
        
        # Register the function with a specific name
        result = self.blueprint.app_template_global("custom_name")(test_func)
        
        # Verify the function is returned unchanged
        self.assertEqual(result, test_func)
        
        # Verify the global was registered (deferred_functions should contain the registration)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 1)

    def test_app_template_global_without_name(self):
        """Test registering a template global without providing a name."""
        def test_func():
            return "global_value"
        
        # Register the function without a specific name
        result = self.blueprint.app_template_global()(test_func)
        
        # Verify the function is returned unchanged
        self.assertEqual(result, test_func)
        
        # Verify the global was registered
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 1)

    def test_app_template_global_as_decorator_with_name(self):
        """Test using app_template_global as a decorator with a name."""
        @self.blueprint.app_template_global("decorator_name")
        def decorated_func():
            return "decorated_value"
        
        # Verify the function is returned correctly
        self.assertTrue(callable(decorated_func))
        
        # Verify the global was registered
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 1)

    def test_app_template_global_as_direct_decorator(self):
        """Test using app_template_global as a direct decorator without parentheses."""
        @self.blueprint.app_template_global
        def direct_decorated_func():
            return "direct_value"
        
        # Verify the function is returned correctly
        self.assertTrue(callable(direct_decorated_func))
        
        # Verify the global was registered
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 1)

    def test_app_template_global_name_with_dot_raises_error(self):
        """Test that providing a name with a dot raises ValueError."""
        def test_func():
            return "global_value"
        
        # Should raise ValueError when name contains a dot
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.blueprint.app_template_global("invalid.name")(test_func)
        
        self.assertIn("'name' may not contain a dot", str(context.exception))

    def test_app_template_global_none_name(self):
        """Test registering a template global with None as name."""
        def test_func():
            return "global_value"
        
        # Register with None name (should use function name)
        result = self.blueprint.app_template_global(None)(test_func)
        
        # Verify the function is returned unchanged
        self.assertEqual(result, test_func)
        
        # Verify the global was registered
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 1)

    def test_multiple_globals_registration(self):
        """Test registering multiple template globals."""
        def func1():
            return "value1"
            
        def func2():
            return "value2"
        
        # Register multiple functions
        self.blueprint.app_template_global("func1")(func1)
        self.blueprint.app_template_global("func2")(func2)
        
        # Verify both were registered
        self.assertEqual(len(self.blueprint.deferred_functions), 2)

    def test_blueprint_initialization_validity(self):
        """Test that blueprint is properly initialized for template global registration."""
        # Verify blueprint has required attributes
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(self.blueprint, 'deferred_functions'))
        self.assertIsInstance(self.blueprint.deferred_functions, list)

from unittest.mock import Mock, patch, MagicMock
import flask
from flask.views import View
from flask.app import Flask


class TestView(View):
    def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs):
        return f"Response with {kwargs}"


class TestViewAsync(View):
    async def dispatch_request(self, **kwargs):
        return f"Async response with {kwargs}"


class TestViewNoDispatch(View):
    pass


class TestViewInitError(View):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__()
        if 'error' in kwargs:
            raise TypeError("Init error")


class TestViewMethod(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self.app = Flask(__name__)

    def test_view_with_valid_view_class(self):
        with self.app.test_request_context():
            # Arrange
            flask.current_app.view_functions['test'] = lambda: None
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.push()
            
            # Act & Assert
            with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestView):
                result = flask.views.view(key1='value1', key2='value2')
                self.assertEqual(result, "Response with {'key1': 'value1', 'key2': 'value2'}")
            
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.pop()

    def test_view_with_async_view_class(self):
        with self.app.test_request_context():
            # Arrange
            flask.current_app.view_functions['test'] = lambda: None
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.push()
            
            # Act & Assert
            with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestViewAsync):
                result = flask.views.view(async_key='async_value')
                # Since we're in sync context, this should still work through ensure_sync
                self.assertIn('async_value', str(result))
            
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.pop()

    def test_view_with_no_dispatch_method(self):
        with self.app.test_request_context():
            # Arrange
            flask.current_app.view_functions['test'] = lambda: None
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.push()
            
            # Act & Assert
            with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestViewNoDispatch):
                with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
                    flask.views.view()
            
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.pop()

    def test_view_with_init_error(self):
        with self.app.test_request_context():
            # Arrange
            flask.current_app.view_functions['test'] = lambda: None
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.push()
            
            # Act & Assert
            with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestViewInitError):
                with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
                    flask.views.view(error=True)
            
            flask.globals._app_ctx_stack.pop()

    def test_view_with_no_current_app(self):
        # Act & Assert
        with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestView):
            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                flask.views.view(test_arg='test_value')

    @patch('flask.views.current_app')
    def test_view_with_ensure_sync_failure(self, mock_current_app):
        with self.app.test_request_context():
            # Arrange
            mock_current_app.ensure_sync = Mock(side_effect=RuntimeError("ensure_sync failed"))
            
            # Act & Assert
            with patch('flask.views.view_class', TestView):
                with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
                    flask.views.view()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import unittest
from unittest.mock import Mock, MagicMock
from flask.sansio.blueprints import Blueprint

class TestAppUrlValuePreprocessor(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        """Set up test fixtures before each test method."""
        self.blueprint = Blueprint('test_blueprint', '__main__')
        self.mock_app = Mock()
        self.mock_app.url_value_preprocessors = []
        self.blueprint.app = self.mock_app
        
    def test_app_url_value_preprocessor_registers_function(self):
        """Test that the preprocessor function is registered with the app."""
        # Arrange
        mock_preprocessor = Mock()
        
        # Act
        result = self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(mock_preprocessor)
        
        # Assert
        self.mock_app.url_value_preprocessors.append.assert_called_once_with(mock_preprocessor)
        self.assertEqual(result, mock_preprocessor)
        
    def test_app_url_value_preprocessor_returns_original_function(self):
        """Test that the method returns the original preprocessor function."""
        # Arrange
        mock_preprocessor = Mock()
        
        # Act
        result = self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(mock_preprocessor)
        
        # Assert
        self.assertIs(result, mock_preprocessor)
        
    def test_app_url_value_preprocessor_multiple_calls(self):
        """Test that multiple calls register multiple preprocessors."""
        # Arrange
        mock_preprocessor1 = Mock()
        mock_preprocessor2 = Mock()
        
        # Act
        result1 = self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(mock_preprocessor1)
        result2 = self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(mock_preprocessor2)
        
        # Assert
        expected_calls = [
            unittest.mock.call(mock_preprocessor1),
            unittest.mock.call(mock_preprocessor2)
        ]
        self.mock_app.url_value_preprocessors.append.assert_has_calls(expected_calls)
        self.assertIs(result1, mock_preprocessor1)
        self.assertIs(result2, mock_preprocessor2)
        
    def test_app_url_value_preprocessor_with_lambda(self):
        """Test that the method works with lambda functions."""
        # Arrange
        lambda_preprocessor = lambda endpoint, values: None
        
        # Act
        result = self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(lambda_preprocessor)
        
        # Assert
        self.mock_app.url_value_preprocessors.append.assert_called_once_with(lambda_preprocessor)
        self.assertIs(result, lambda_preprocessor)
        
    def test_app_url_value_preprocessor_with_none_app(self):
        """Test behavior when app is None (should raise AttributeError)."""
        # Arrange
        self.blueprint.app = None
        mock_preprocessor = Mock()
        
        # Act & Assert
        with self.assertRaises(AttributeError):
            self.blueprint.app_url_value_preprocessor(mock_preprocessor)

            return s.lower()

        # Register the filter without providing a name
        self.app.add_template_filter(lowercase_filter)

        # Check that the filter is registered under its function name
        self.assertIn("lowercase_filter", self.app.jinja_env.filters)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.jinja_env.filters["lowercase_filter"], lowercase_filter)

    def test_add_multiple_filters(self) -> None:
        # Define two filter functions

            return s[::-1]

        def capitalize_filter(s: str) -> str:
            return s.capitalize()

        # Register both filters
        self.app.add_template_filter(reverse_filter, name="reverse")
        self.app.add_template_filter(capitalize_filter, name="capitalize")

        # Check that both filters are registered correctly
        self.assertIn("reverse", self.app.jinja_env.filters)
        self.assertIn("capitalize", self.app.jinja_env.filters)

        """Test loads with a valid JSON string."""
        data = '{"name": "John", "age": 30}'
        result = loads(data)
        expected = {"name": "John", "age": 30}
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)

    def test_loads_with_valid_json_bytes(self):
        """Test loads with valid JSON bytes."""
        data = b'{"name": "John", "age": 30}'
        result = loads(data)
        expected = {"name": "John", "age": 30}
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)

    def test_loads_with_additional_kwargs(self):
        """Test loads passes additional kwargs to underlying implementation."""
        data = '{"name": "John", "age": 30}'
        result = loads(data, parse_float=str)
        # When parse_float=str, floats are returned as strings
        expected = {"name": "John", "age": "30"}
        self.assertEqual(result, expected)

    def test_loads_uses_current_app_when_available(self, mock_app_ctx):

            data = '{"test": "data"}'
            result = loads(data)
            expected = {"custom": "implementation"}
